local_facts.title: Proposition 213 is a distinct vehicle-claim rule
local_facts.claim: California Civil Code section 3333.4 limits non-economic losses in specified motor-vehicle cases involving an uninsured owner or an operator unable to establish required financial responsibility; the statute lists pain, suffering, inconvenience, impairment, and disfigurement among those losses and includes a defined exception.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Long Beach crash file should preserve insurance and ownership records at the outset. This rule can change the analysis independently of who caused the collision.

local_facts.title: Long Beach maintains designated truck routes
local_facts.claim: The City of Long Beach truck-route map identifies designated truck routes and shows harbor-area streets plus freeway connections including the 710, 405, 91, 605, and 103.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A collision involving a port-serving or other commercial vehicle may require early preservation of carrier identity, trailer details, and business-held records in addition to the usual crash evidence.

local_facts.title: Civil trial departments are listed in Long Beach
local_facts.claim: Los Angeles Superior Court’s civil trial courtroom list identifies Long Beach civil trial departments S10, S28, and S29 at 275 Magnolia Avenue, Long Beach, California 90802.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Court procedure and venue are case-specific, but a Long Beach claim is usually heard at a courthouse near the city, on that court's own calendar and deadlines.

pricing.table_head: What the contract has to say, and what the courthouse collects
pricing.col_b: What the statute or schedule requires

anchors.label: Sentence the contract itself must contain
anchors.detail: Outside medical negligence claims, California requires a contingency contract to state that the fee is not set by law but is negotiable between attorney and client.

anchors.label: Percentage ceiling on an ordinary injury fee
anchors.detail: The State Bar rule prohibits an unconscionable or illegal fee and supplies thirteen factors for testing one. It assigns no percentage to a negligence recovery.
anchors.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(a)-(b)

anchors.label: First paper where the claim stays at or under $12,500
anchors.detail: The Los Angeles Superior Court draws its limited-civil line at $12,500 rather than the $10,000 figure printed on schedules elsewhere in California.

anchors.label: Electronic filing service fee, charged per transaction
anchors.detail: Added to each eFiling transaction in Los Angeles civil cases under the Rules of Court provisions governing electronic filing and service.

fee_rows.stage: The contingency share in a Long Beach injury claim
fee_rows.note: Unconscionability is judged on the facts existing when the agreement was made, weighing proportion to the value of services, relative sophistication, results obtained, and informed consent.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5(b)

fee_rows.note: It states the rate, how disbursements and costs affect both the fee and the recovery, compensation for related matters, and the negotiability statement.

fee_rows.stage: A contract that leaves out a required term
fee_rows.note: The client may void it, after which the attorney is entitled only to a reasonable fee rather than the percentage the contract named.

fee_rows.stage: Claims against a health care provider, a different statute
fee_rows.note: That schedule governs professional negligence actions against health care providers only, and higher rates require a motion showing good cause.

fee_rows.stage: Workers' compensation fees, a separate track
fee_rows.share: Approved by the appeals board first
fee_rows.note: No fee may be demanded or accepted from an injured employee until the appeals board approves or sets the amount, and the contingency contract statute excludes comp.

fee_rows.stage: Dividing the fee with another firm
fee_rows.note: The lawyers need a written agreement, the client consents in writing after full written disclosure, and the total fee cannot rise because of the division.
fee_rows.source_name: Cal. Rules of Prof. Conduct, rule 1.5.1(a)
